# Incident Report: Koi Stealer Infection — 2024-09-04

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** |
| AD domain | BEPOSITIVE (bepositive.com, DC = WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com at 172.17.0.17) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **afletcher** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `afletcher`, realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM`) |

Identified from the DHCP Discover/Request (`dhcp.option.hostname = DESKTOP-RNVO9AT`, offered 172.17.0.99), the ARP reply binding that IP to MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4, NBNS name registrations (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`, `BEPOSITIVE<00>`), and Kerberos traffic to the domain controller.

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer), an HTTP-based information stealer.

- **Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The provided IDS export shows `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` firing 48 times against 172.17.0.99 <-> 79.124.78.197.
- **Also behaviorally confirmed** independent of the alert: manual inspection of the TCP streams shows repeated `POST /foots.php` beacons with the exact payload format `<opcode>|<bot-GUID>|<random-token>|<base64-blob>`, e.g. `101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=`, repeating on a ~60-90 second interval with a static bot GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` — consistent, structured C2 telemetry rather than a one-off false positive.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the pcap)

### Command-and-control
- **79.124.78.197:80** (HTTP) — primary Koi Stealer C2. Endpoints:
  - `POST /foots.php` — periodic beacon/checkin, 48 occurrences from 2024-09-04 17:35:07 UTC through the end of the capture (17:35 – 18:32 UTC window), interval ~60-90s.
  - `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — returned `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`, a pay-per-install/affiliate-style redirect token (subid), consistent with malware delivered through a PPI distribution network.
  - `POST /index.php` — returned an encrypted binary blob (likely config/exfil channel).
  - No DNS lookup precedes any connection to 79.124.78.197 — the malware connects to this C2 by hardcoded IP literal, bypassing DNS-based detection.

- **Malicious/staging domain: www.bellantonicioccolato.it (46.254.34.201:443)** — two back-to-back TLS sessions (17:34:57–17:36:39 UTC) transferring ~719 KB down to the host, starting ~2 seconds before the first Koi Stealer beacon. No DNS query for this domain appears in the capture either. Content is TLS-encrypted (TLS 1.3 application data), so no filename/hash could be extracted from this session, but the timing and volume are consistent with this being the payload-staging/loader delivery leg immediately preceding stealer activation on an otherwise-legitimate (likely compromised) site.

### Malware User-Agent
`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)` — used on every `/foots.php` beacon request. This is an anachronistic forged IE7-on-Trident string, not the host's actual browser UA, and functions as a fingerprint for the malicious process's HTTP requests.

### Files / hashes
**None recoverable.** No executable, script, or archive was transferred in the clear over HTTP in this capture (`--export-objects http` yielded only benign items: Microsoft `connecttest.txt`, Adobe `ProcessMAU.txt`, and the stealer's own encrypted `index.php`/`foots.php` bodies). The likely payload delivery occurred over TLS to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, which this capture cannot decrypt. No SHA256 can be stated without fabricating one.

## 4. Alerts assessed as benign / false positives (not evidence of compromise)

- `ET INFO Terse Request for .txt` / `ET INFO Microsoft Connection Test` vs 23.220.251.149 — this is legitimate Windows NCSI connectivity check (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`), not hostile.
- `ET POLICY Reserved Internal IP Traffic`, DNS NXDOMAIN alerts, SMBv1/NTLMSSP/IPC$/kerberos-overflow signatures — all traffic exclusively between 172.17.0.99 and the internal domain controller 172.17.0.17 (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19), consisting of standard SMB negotiate/session-setup, DFS referral, and Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic for domain logon. No lateral movement, no internal file access beyond IPC$ pipe negotiation, no exploitation payload observed in these streams.

## 5. Summary

DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), used by domain user `afletcher` on the BEPOSITIVE domain, downloaded a payload via TLS from the likely-compromised site `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) at 17:34:57 UTC, then began periodic encrypted beacon traffic to Koi Stealer C2 `79.124.78.197:80` (`/foots.php`, `/index.php`) starting 17:35:07 UTC and continuing for the remainder of the capture (~55 minutes, 48 checkins). Attribution to Koi Stealer is both signature-confirmed (ETPRO rule) and behaviorally confirmed (beacon format, bot GUID, cadence). No malware binary or hash could be extracted since delivery and C2 traffic are TLS/encrypted-payload based.
